title: Patchcraft: voice synthesis & action catalog (quickpatch + backlog)
content:
TL;DR:
- This is a compact synthesis of ~58 customer threads (support, CSM notes, and Slack) collected 2026-07-20 -> 2026-07-29. Goal: identify low-risk quickpatches that buy time and a prioritized backlog for product/eng.

Signal sources and weighting:
- 26 support tickets (priority: medium)
- 18 CSM field notes (high-touch enterprise customers)
- 8 Slack threads (dev-community + early adopters)
- 6 product feedback forms (qual + quant)
- Weighting: enterprise voice > recurring dev threads > one-off support logs.

Observed themes (high level):
1) Latency spikes with long-context chat sessions (hosted-api). Users see 2-3x token latency after KV cache warmup misses.
2) KV cache invalidation surprises on rollouts/canaries — customer apps experience stale prompt artifacts or increased tails.
3) Embedding consistency and billing surprise: small customers confused by sub-token rounding and embedding batch sizing.
4) Private deployment onboarding friction: networking/KMS docs missing step-by-step for common cloud providers.
5) Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution exists but customers want per-route lineage + example inputs that triggered regressions.
6) Autoscale burst behavior for Dedicated: some customers see brief request errors when burst policy transitions.

Top asks (prioritized by frequency + impact):
A. Fast-fail and fallback policy for KV cache cold misses (mentions: 28 threads). Impact: reduces tail latency/regressions for chat apps.
B. Embedding batch-size guidance + UI example with cost estimate (mentions: 17 threads). Impact: reduces billing confusion and support load.
C. Private install quickstart per-cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) with KMS checklist (mentions: 14 threads). Impact: reduces onboarding time by ~2–4 days.
D. Per-route input-to-output trace view (mentions: 12 threads). Impact: debug speed for customers + less need for data exports.
E. Dedicated burst policy visualization + recommended guardrails (mentions: 9 threads). Impact: fewer transient 5xxs during scale events.

Quickpatches (can ship in 1–2 sprints, low-risk):
1) KV-cold fast-fail toggle (owner: eng-serving-runtime) — default off, opt-in via header for beta customers. Behavior: detect >x KV misses in last y tokens and fall back to smaller context window or different model variant rather than blocking. Estimated effort: 3 engineer-days + 1 QA. Acceptance criteria: reduces 95th percentile latency on a synthetic chat replay by 30%.
2) Embedding-cost explainer snippet in Console (owner: product-hosted-api) — UI copy + example batch calculator. Estimated effort: 2 PM-days + 2 design-days + 1 eng-day. Acceptance criteria: 30% drop in support tickets about embedding billing in next 30 days for pilot cohort.
3) Private-deploy KMS common-issues FAQ (owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services) — doc + quick CLI commands for IAM roles. Estimated effort: 2 writer-days + 1 SE-day. Acceptance criteria: <3 clarified follow-ups on pilot installs.

Medium-term backlog (scoped, 1–3 months):
- Per-route trace & replay tool (console + API) — heavy infra/telemetry work. Cross-team: observability + product + eng (estimate: 6–8 sprints).
- Autoscale transition smoothing for Dedicated — integrate leaky-bucket warmup with routing fallback. Owner: infra + platform-engineering (estimate: 4 sprints).
- Rollout-safe KV cache invalidation primitives — atomic invalidation hooks + canary-aware cache TTLs. Owner: serving-runtime + release-engineering (estimate: 3 sprints).
- Embedding batch optimizer in Redwood Optimize (suggested feature) — offline suggestion engine + live UI. Owner: optimize team (estimate: 5 sprints).

Risk and tradeoffs:
- Quickpatch fast-fail for KV reduces tail latency but can change model output fidelity (smaller context or variant). Must be opt-in and clearly communicated.
- Embedding UI guidance reduces confusion but may hide deeper API-level billing mismatches; we need telemetry to confirm impact.
- Per-route traces carry PII risk — must ensure scrub/pseudonymization and opt-in logging. Coordinate with security/compliance.

Concrete mappings (who to ping):
- KV fast-fail spike: @Marco Ruiz (eng-serving-runtime), ENG-7893 (linked).
- Embedding explainer & calculator: @Priya Singh (product-hosted-api), GH PR stub: /runtime/pull/342.
- Private quickstart / KMS: @Evan Cole (solutions-engineering).
- Trace/replay feature: @Lina Park (observability).

Metrics to watch (post-change):
- 95th and 99th percentile token latency on chat routes (daily), by customer tier.
- Support ticket volume on embedding & billing (weekly).
- Time-to-onboard (private deploy) measured by days from contract to first successful inference.
- Rate of Dedicated transient 5xxs during bursts.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP quickpatches):
- KV fast-fail: 95th percentile latency improved by >=25% for affected customers in pilot. No more than 5% change in semantic similarity on canned prompts (internal eval).
- Embedding explainer: pilot group support tickets drop by >=30% in 45 days.
- Private quickstart doc: first three pilot installs complete without SE phone assistance.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- For KV fast-fail heuristic: what threshold (x misses, y tokens) balances fidelity vs tail reduction? Need A/B with synthetic replays.
- Do we want a telemetry opt-in for per-route traces or built-in redaction by default? Security will want opt-in + audit.
- Embedding rounding: can we change billing granularity at backend or only address via education? Finance + billing needed.

Next steps (owner Aisha):
1) Spin up a 2-week fastpatch squad: Marco + 1 runtime eng + 1 QA — goal: prototype KV fast-fail and test on 3 pilot customers (start: 2026-08-11).
2) Product to draft embedding explainer & calculator copy for Console (Priya) by 2026-08-12.
3) Solutions eng to publish Private KMS quickstart draft by 2026-08-13 and collect pilot feedback.
4) Schedule cross-team sync (observability + infra + serving-runtime) to scope trace work (target meeting 2026-08-17).

Notes to self / conversational fragments captured from threads:
- "We saw a weird jump in latency after deploy — felt like cache got flushed but no rollout was scheduled." — fintech-customer
- "Embedding costs spiked after we naively batched 300 at once — we expected linear scaling — why are we billed so much?" — marketplace startup
- "Private installer doc assumed corporate KMS knowledge; our infra team got stuck on service account perms." — enterprise pilot

Appendix: raw signal index (short):
- CS-1452: repeated latency report from customer X (ticket excerpt noted above).
- ENG-7893: runtime change that touched cache TTLs in July; possible correlation.
- GH PR /runtime/pull/342: small console change that added token-level cost view (candidate place to add embedding snippet).

If we want I can convert quickpatch writeups into a PR template for eng and a single-slide exec note for leadership. Otherwise this sits as the field-curated backlog for August sprint planning.

-- Aisha
